utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is the case IT-95-5/18-PT, The Prosecutor versus Radovan Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Karadzic. I note that you appear again without counsel. Can you please confirm to me that you continue to represent yourself.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. This Status Conference was arranged when the process of presenting a motion to amend the indictment was likely to be completed. The motion was filed on the 22nd of September. I understand that you received the translation yesterday, the 27th of October, and it's at that stage that the Court becomes seized of the matter. I wish to, first of all, clarify certain things from the Prosecution point of view before I turn to you for any comments you wish to make on the state of play now that that motion is translated into your language. Mr. Tieger, can you explain to me what supporting material for the motion and the proposed amended indictment, if any, remains unserved or unintimated to the accused.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, as a general matter, the answer is none. I understand, however, there may be a few, that is, a handful of translation, that have not been provided; and there may also be an issue with some of the B/C/S audios that I would need to check often. My understanding previously was that all disclosure had a been provided. I will attend to that immediately.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: B/C/S audios are material in his language. If they have been disclosed in that form, then they've been disclosed in terms of the Rules. I'm more concerned about documents you say are untranslated. Can you clarify the position in regard to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: If the Court will give me just a moment, Your Honour. The best clarification I can provide at this point is that there are no more than four or five, as I understand it; and I will check immediately on the status of those translations and make them a priority, clearly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Do you know whether these are lengthy documents or simple documents?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I do not, at this time, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Rather an unsatisfactory state of affairs, Mr. Tieger, at this stage, I have to say. That is the sort of simple information that this Trial Chamber is entitled to have before it whenever it comes into court. I am about to adjourn to enable you to check the position, and we'll resume when you're able to tell the clerk that that has been done. --- Break taken at 9.04 a.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I gather you have the answer, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Four documents, comprising a total of 60 pages, and those can be provided, I'm told, by Thursday and -- well, Thursday is what I was told so I would say by Friday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Of this week?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Now, Mr. Karadzic, you've got the motion; you've got the proposed indictment. By the end of this week, you will have all the supporting material, which is the basis for the indictment, according to the Prosecution. The next issue is the time for you to respond to this motion, and the normal period to response for a motion of this kind is 14 days. Now, do you have anything to say on that issue?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not for the moment. I don't have anything to say on that issue, but I must say that I'm not prepared for this Status Conference. Yesterday, towards the evening, I received official information or instructions that this Status Conference would be held; and in the media, I heard it on Friday the 24th, and then I submitted a motion on that subject. I also received the indictment yesterday; and, all in all, I have not had time to even look at it because I had a visit and another matters to attend to, so that have I nothing to offer up for today's Status Conference, because, quite simply, I'm not prepared for this conference. I had a lot of work to do, I still do not have a team, and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, I take some responsibility for the situation that led to you receiving formal notification, as you put it, in B/C/S of today's hearing only yesterday; however, I do know that you were aware of the hearing last week and that you did, in fact, make a submission on Friday about it. You're also aware that I tried to take account of other issues that face you at the moment; but, at the same time, this case has to proceed and I'm trying to make an orderly arrangement for the progress this case, taking into account the other commitments that you are faced with at the moment, which are beyond your control, as I understand. I'm giving you the opportunity, now that you are here, to consider what you believe to be a reasonable period to respond. In the absence of a motion, then responses will be due in 14 days, and the Trial Chamber will proceed to deal with the motion for amendment on that basis. If you want to leave it that way, that's a matter for you, and we can adjourn.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do believe that, even for that response, I would have to seek counsel from my legal advisors, I just have just one so far, and I hope that quite soon I will be able to set up my team and will be prepared for Status Conference. As far as speed of work is concerned, I think that in the 120 days that usually elapse, there is usually one Status Conference held that at that period of time; whereas, so far we have four.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So is that all you wish to say?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wasn't even ready to say that today. I quite simply stated that I'm not prepared for today's Status Conference.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, as matters stand, then, from the moment that you receive in B/C/S the supporting material for the motion to amend the indictment, you will have 14 days to respond to that. The only other matter that I have in mind to deal with is fixing the next Status Conference. Now, Mr. Tieger, before I do that, do you have any other matter to raise?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: There is one motion, I note, that certainly passed through my hands yesterday which is for judicial notice of adjudicated facts. I assume that in the same way as you consented to postponement of the motions, the preliminary motions, when the accused sought that a decision that he need not respond until the question of the indictment had been resolved, that would also be your position in relation to the motion for judicial notice of adjudicated facts.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That's fine, Your Honour, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So there are these two issues, Mr. Karadzic. You requested that you need not submit preliminary motions until after the whole issue of indictment was resolved and the Trial Chamber agreed to that. The same is the position in relation to the motion which has just submitted, you may not have received it, which is for judicial notice of adjudicated facts. You can take it that the Trial Chamber will not address that issue until the whole issue of the indictment has been resolved. Now, is there any other matter that you wish to raise before I fix the date for the next Status Conference?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I want to say that I've already traversed a certain path without my Defence team. I have gone a certain way towards my Defence, but I will have -- be facing problems. I don't have the necessary resources, I don't have a Defence team, and with the speed at which matters are progressing in these proceedings, I am afraid that I will be in an even less equal position, and I'd like to you be aware of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I'm astonished at your reference to speed. I'm extremely disappointed at the very slow rate at which this case is proceeding. You were in custody from, at the latest, the 21st of July. I think you suggest it was even earlier than that, and you were here on the 30th of July. We're only now at the stage of considering a motion to amend the indictment which the Prosecution hope will be the indictment on which the trial progresses. That's a period of three months, and we've gone virtually nowhere. Rest assured, that is not a fast rate of speed for any court to progress. It's your own choice, as you know very well, that you represent yourself, and I'm afraid that carries particular problems which you've been told about repeatedly. You're willing to take on your own shoulders, and that is a matter for you at this stage. So, in these circumstances, we will adjourn now and the next Status Conference is likely to be - there will be a written order confirming it, but you can put it in your diary - it is likely to be on Tuesday, the 20th of January.
